purpose: Coverage for every lockfile package whose own npm tarball ships no license text. Read by scripts/third-party-notices.mjs, which re-verifies every SHA-256 below on each run and fails if one changes.
howToUpdate: Add or edit an entry here and re-run `npm run notices`. Do not edit the texts in this directory unless upstream changed them; the generator validates the recorded hash.

evidence: The registry reports gitHead 208f539945b145e7c9d6d844290f81c3fe5af320 for both esbuild@0.25.12 and every @esbuild/* platform package at 0.25.12: they are built from one revision of one project.

The LICENSE.md fetched from that revision through the GitHub contents API is byte-identical (SHA-256 b40ec5ba…) to esbuild-0.25.12-LICENSE.md, which is copied from the installed esbuild@0.25.12 tarball — a package whose integrity is pinned in package-lock.json.
The platform packages' own tarballs contain only package.json, README.md and the binary; that is why no text is available from them directly.

fsevents is an optional dependency for macOS only (required by chokidar, rollup, tsx and vite), so it is in the lockfile but is not installed on this Windows machine.
The upstream repository at that revision contains a 1133-byte LICENSE with the project's own MIT text and copyright line, reproduced here unmodified.
The package declares "license": "MIT" in its package.json, and the registry reports the same for this version (gitHead 80dfaef91ee87008f4ed2b6e78921d383bccd406).

The tarball, integrity-verified against package-lock.json, contains only index.js, test.js, package.json and Readme.md — no license file. Neither does the repository at that revision, nor its default branch.

Its README at that revision links http://jsumners.mit-license.org/, which serves the MIT text at /license.txt. That URL returned HTTP 200 text/plain, and the 1112 bytes it returned are reproduced here verbatim, with SHA-256 af15a41ce02371f77476b7a201e036c0ae6c5d6d2a233b4e5f0fd5fca123457e.

The notice's year is generated by that endpoint when it is requested, so the year in this copy is a retrieval snapshot (2026-10-16) and is not a publication date of the package. The endpoint renders from a pinned per-author config in remy/mit-license — commit 21ac30f351903ff23b399289cb4fdda05fb45f15, blob ecd7b38c6127119bcf98e6429660d02edf9d5c57 — which names the copyright holder (James Sumners). No wording and no name was added or altered here.

This is the license text the publisher's own package documentation points at, for this exact version. It is vendored as the upstream-linked text; a distributor relying on it should read the recorded URL and hashes rather than this summary.

evidence: The package declares "license": "MIT" in its package.json, and the registry reports the same for this version (gitHead e636db817a96e4ca4710b407163fb992748b3b80).

No license text was retrievable from any of these, each checked directly: the published tarball (package.json, index.js, README.md and five files under dist/ — integrity verified against package-lock.json); the repository at that revision (.gitignore, .travis.yml, README.md, index.js, package.json, test.js); the repository's default branch; and the link its README gives for licensing.

That link, oss.ninja/mit/developit, redirects to an unrelated site: the response body is a 141 KB HTML page that is not this package's license text. Fetching it therefore proves nothing either way, and it was not copied — vendoring unrelated third-party page output as a license would misrepresent it.

So the position is: the declared license is MIT and a retrievable text was not found at any of the four places checked. That is a retrieval result, not a statement that the publisher never issued a license, and the gap stays open until text is found or the dependency is removed.
